```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
library(data.table)
library(dplyr)
library(broom)
library(tibble)
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
```


This code goes through performing linear regression models to see if the baseline alpha diversity measure predict change in clicial outcomes (e.g., do the microbiome in your gut prior to the interveniton predict weight loss during the intervention you may lose during the intervention)


### Load in data
```{r}
meta <- fread("C:/Users/jhres/Documents/DRIFT2/Week3/DRIFT_long_metadata_microbiome_092026.csv")
meta_wide <- fread("C:/Users/jhres/Documents/DRIFT2/Week3/DRIFT_wide_metadata_microbiome_092026.csv")
```

```{r}
#prep data

meta_wide$Intervention<- factor(meta_wide$Intervention, lev=c('IMF', 'DCR'))

meta_wide$imf<- factor(meta_wide$imf, lev=c('1','0'))
# 1 (IMF) is referent 

meta_wide$race_cat_3<- factor(meta_wide$race_cat_3, lev=c('White','Black/African American', 'Other'))

meta_wide$race_3<- factor(meta_wide$race_3, lev=c('0', '1', '2'))

table(meta_wide$sex)
meta_wide$sex <- factor(meta_wide$sex, lev=c('0','1'))

meta_wide$ethnicity<- factor(meta_wide$ethnicity, lev=c('0','1'))

#standardize the alpha diversity measures to have a mean of 0 and sd of 1
#this will make plots later look nicer and have consistent axes for easier comparison between measures

colSums(is.na(meta_wide[, c('pielou_evenness_BL', 'shannon_entropy_BL', 'faith_pd_BL', 'observed_features_BL')])) #check for missing data
meta_standardized <- meta_wide %>% filter(is.na(pielou_evenness_BL)==F, is.na(shannon_entropy_BL)==F, is.na(faith_pd_BL)==F, is.na(observed_features_BL)==F)
#this removes the 5 missing BL stool samples ... N=145 now

mean(meta_standardized$shannon_entropy_BL) #not 0 (or close to 0)
sd(meta_standardized$shannon_entropy) #not 1 (or close to 1)

meta_standardized <- meta_standardized %>% mutate_at(c('pielou_evenness_BL', 'shannon_entropy_BL', 'faith_pd_BL', 'observed_features_BL'), ~(scale(.) %>% as.vector))

mean(meta_standardized$pielou_evenness_BL)
sd(meta_standardized$pielou_evenness_BL)

```

### Regression models
Do BL alpha diversity measures predict change in weight from BL to 3m

```{r}
#easiet way is to make a new dataset with only timepoints of interest
#meta_standardized
#meta.bl.3 <- meta_standardized %>% filter(Timepoint=='BL' | Timepoint=='3m')
#meta.bl.3 <- meta.bl.3 %>% group_by(subject_id)
#meta.bl.3 <- meta.bl.3 %>% filter(n() == 2)
#meta.bl.3 <- ungroup(meta.bl.3)
#meta.bl.3 <- as.data.frame(meta.bl.3)
 
#meta.3 <-  meta.bl.3 %>% filter(Timepoint=='3m')
#meta.bl <-  meta.bl.3 %>% filter(Timepoint=='BL')
```


```{r}
#here is a VERY basic regression model (outcome ~ predictor) that does not include any covariates (e.g., things that you control for in the models)

# ******** This is the key variable that we are editing to add covariance**********
shannon_wt <- lm(
  change_outcome_wt_fnl_3m_BL ~ shannon_entropy_BL + race_3 + ethnicity, 
  data = meta_standardized) # + to add each covariant into the model
shannon_wt


# the output (shannon_wt) is a list of 13, so we will use summary() to more easily view the results
shannon_wt #gives you the formula and coeffiecents for the variables

summary(shannon_wt) #gives you more info
# we are not interested in the intercept data

summary(shannon_wt)$coefficients[2,] #gives only values for shannon


shannon_wt$coefficients #these are the betas
confint(shannon_wt) #these are the betas
shannon_wt_df <- data.frame(summary(shannon_wt)$coefficients,
                             confint(shannon_wt))
#pull the beta estimate and 95% confidence intervals and put them into a dataframe
shannon_wt_df <- data.frame(summary(shannon_wt)$coefficients,
                             confint(shannon_wt)) %>%
                      dplyr::rename(p.value = Pr...t..,
                                    LCL = X2.5..,
                                    UCL = X97.5..)

shannon_wt_df <- data.frame(summary(shannon_wt)$coefficients,  #pull the coefficent table
                             confint(shannon_wt)) %>%          #get the confidence intervals
                      dplyr::rename(p.value = Pr...t..,        #rename vairables 
                                    LCL = X2.5..,
                                    UCL = X97.5..) %>%
                      tibble::rownames_to_column("term") %>%  #originally the "terms" (i.e., the intercept and any predictor variables or covariates were rownames)
                      dplyr::filter(term != "(Intercept, race_31, race_32)")    #select the variables of interest or filter out those that are not of interest 

shannon_wt_df

#or all in one simple step using broom
shannon_wt_df <- tidy(shannon_wt, conf.int = TRUE) %>%
                      dplyr::filter(term == "shannon_entropy_BL")

#you can rename these column names or leave them as is
```


### Forest plots

This is a forest plot showing the beta coefficent ("estimate"). Here we can see the direction of effect (positive beta value on the right side of the dashed line at 0 indicating no effect). The confidence interval extends from the point (a short line = more precise). Since our CI crosses the 0 on the x-axis, BL shannon does not predict change in weight from BL to 3m (also seen in the p-value which is >0.05). The non-sigificant value is represnted by an open circle.

```{r}

shannon_wt_df <- shannon_wt_df %>%
  mutate(outcome = "Weight",     #will be the label for the x-axis
         sig = ifelse(p.value < 0.05, "Sig", "N.S."))   #for indicating if the p-value is significant

alpha_plot <- ggplot(shannon_wt_df, aes(x = outcome, y = estimate)) +    #outcome on the "x-axis" and beta on the "y-axis" ... we flip the plot later
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 'dashed', color = 'grey20') +    #gives the dashed line at "y-intercept" of 0 ... we flip the plot to have this on the x-axis
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = conf.low, ymax = conf.high),
                width = 0.05, size = 1.3) +    #adds the confidence interval line
  geom_point(aes(shape = sig), size = 9, color = "#5FA3CC") +     # this is the point/beta - shape, size, and color of the circles
  coord_flip() +  #flip plot
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(1, 19)) +     # N.S. = open circles, Sig = solid/filled in circles
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Beta Coefficient", shape = "Significance") +
  theme_bw() +      #makes it a clean looking plot (white background)
  theme(        #additional theme options (e.g., text sizes)
    axis.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 14),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 14),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 12),
    plot.margin = margin(t = 10, r = 15, b = 10, l = 15, unit = "pt")
  )
alpha_plot


#ggsave(alpha_plot, file='/Users/ashleyward/Desktop/DRIFT2_microbiome/manuscript/PATH//DRIFT_alpha_diversity_shannon_lm_overall_change_outcomes_092026.png', device='png', units='in', width=17, height=12, dpi=900)
```
